new_description: Compact deflector emitter for shuttles and runabouts. It holds a single modulated shield frequency in the megahertz range, the same band as the shields of larger Starfleet ships. Good protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet fighter shields, size for size, it draws the least power, but holds the least energy.

The emitter steps through a rotating shield frequency, so an enemy that has matched one harmonic is thrown off at the next. Good protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet fighter shields, size for size, it recharges the fastest, but draws the most power.

A test emitter that carries the shield harmonics on a tighter subspace field. It is a prototype, and the engineers still tune it by hand. Good protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet fighter shields, size for size, it is the quickest to come back after being knocked down and draws the least power.

Borrows the subspace compression pulse of transphasic weapons for its field, with a randomised phase pattern across the grid. An enemy has no steady frequency to learn. Strong protection against beams and energy fire. Of the Starfleet fighter shields, size for size, it holds the most energy and covers the widest area, but draws the most power.

A simple deflector generator for cargo haulers and tenders. It is built to turn away debris and the odd raider. Strong protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet ship shields, size for size, it draws the least power and is the lightest, but holds the least energy.

The standard deflector generator of Starfleet escorts and patrol craft, with its emitters modulated across a narrow frequency band. Good protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet ship shields, size for size, it covers the narrowest area.

A multiphasic grid, the advanced Federation deflector type that also shields against subspace radiation and the energy emissions of stars. Strong protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet ship shields, size for size, it recharges the fastest and is the quickest to come back after being knocked down, but is the costliest to build.
The main deflector grid of Starfleet cruisers, with its emitters spread over the hull to keep the field even. Strong protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds.

The grid reads incoming fire and remodulates its shield harmonics to match, so each hit lands on a field already tuned against it. Strong protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet ship shields, size for size, it is the quickest to come back after being knocked down.

Shield emitters set in a hardened housing and tied into the hull's structural integrity field, so the emitters survive a hit that breaks the shield. Strong protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds.

A canopy field drawn over the largest hulls from a ring of emitters, with the harmonics phase-locked across the whole span. Strong protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet ship shields, size for size, it is the slowest to come back after being knocked down.

An experimental canopy that applies transphasic subspace compression to the field. The phase configuration is randomised so it cannot be predicted. Strong protection against beams and energy fire. Weak against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet ship shields, size for size, it holds the most energy and covers the widest area, but draws the most power.

A deflector for pickets and defence stations, powered from the station's own grid. Strong protection against kinetic rounds, beams, energy fire and plasma. Of the Starfleet platform shields, size for size, it holds the most energy and recharges the fastest, but covers the narrowest area.

A platform deflector with its emitters phase-locked into one field. Strong protection against kinetic rounds, beams, energy fire and plasma. Of the Starfleet platform shields, size for size, it is the lightest and the cheapest to build, but holds the least energy.

A transphasic shield for the largest platforms, with a subspace compression pulse that randomises the phase of the field. Strong protection against kinetic rounds, beams, energy fire and plasma. Of the Starfleet platform shields, size for size, it covers the widest area, but draws the most power.

A shield emitter for outposts and relay stations, tied to the station's structural integrity field. Strong protection against kinetic rounds, beams, energy fire and plasma. Of the Starfleet station shields, size for size, it draws the least power and is the cheapest to build, but holds the least energy.

The main deflector array of a Starbase, with emitters on every pylon and rotating shield harmonics. Strong protection against kinetic rounds, beams, energy fire and plasma. Of the Starfleet station shields, size for size, it has the sturdiest housing, but draws the most power.

The full shield grid of a large Starbase, with multiphasic emitters across the ring and the docking arms. Strong protection against kinetic rounds, beams, energy fire and plasma. Of the Starfleet station shields, size for size, it holds the most energy and is the lightest.

The deflector of the great Spacedock stations, with adaptive harmonics that follow every ship in the docking zone. Strong protection against kinetic rounds, beams, energy fire and plasma. Of the Starfleet station shields, size for size, it recharges the fastest and covers the widest area, but is the costliest to build.
